answer.sameness: Most desktop pages use a thin header, a large left-aligned headline with compact supporting text and a small rectangular button, plus one image or illustration on the right. Kolesarski servis, Pivovarna and Plesna šola are particularly close: near-black backgrounds, heavy white sans-serif headlines, isolated artwork and coloured horizontal bands. The same bold sans-serif treatment dominates most businesses; Atelje, Urarstvo and Vinarstvo switch to serif headlines. On phones, nearly every page becomes the same narrow stack beneath an outlined menu button, with a bottom call/directions bar. Business-specific colours and subjects provide more differentiation than the underlying layouts.
recurringIssues: Several hero images feel like decorative placeholders rather than persuasive evidence of the business, particularly the brewery chain, cycling contours and schematic dance footsteps.
Mobile layouts largely stack desktop components without sufficiently reprioritising them; the glass photograph pushes the main proposition below most of the first screen.
Repeated heavy headlines and tightly broken lines make unrelated businesses share the same visual voice.
Desktop navigation, supporting text and buttons are frequently undersized relative to the headline and available space.
The repeated bottom action bars crowd the mobile viewport, leaving awkward fragments of subsequent content visible above them.

best.why: The forest-green and brass palette, serif typography and detailed watch mechanism form the set's most coherent business-specific identity.
The lavender ground, expressive serif headline and overlapping vineyard photography create a more distinctive editorial composition than the standard split heroes.
The strong green-and-yellow palette and oversized cheese illustration create an immediately recognisable identity with clear hierarchy on both screen sizes.

weakest.why: The blurry chain image contributes little appeal or brewery character, leaving a generic dark hero whose large headline does almost all the work.
The tall glass-storage photograph and excessively long headline compete on desktop, while the photo-first mobile order delays the core proposition substantially.
The contour artwork and dark split layout could belong to many outdoor businesses, with little visible cycling-specific character beyond the text.

answer.oneChange: Require a genuinely business-specific hero concept for every project—using its own composition and credible visual evidence—before applying the shared responsive components.
answer.summary: This is a competent template-shop portfolio with several promising identities, not yet a consistently bespoke studio offering. Colour choices and a few serif-led designs create variety, but too many pages share the same headline, button and decorative-image formula. Urarstvo, Vinarstvo and Sirarna show stronger art direction. The weakest work substitutes loosely relevant imagery for a compelling view of the business. Mobile execution is generally legible, but stacking alone does not always preserve priorities. Invest first in distinct hero concepts and stronger business-specific imagery rather than further palette variations.
